texts: On day 270 of Year 1, the village held the summer feast at midsummer.
The keepers of Aelmere ate together at the village square at midday.
The Council toasted the investiture of Coraline Ash.
The Council toasted the investiture of Mira.
Mira had completed her apprenticeship at the summer solstice.

q1_issues.issue: The past perfect "had completed" gets (Past sk_complete_1) but no (Before sk_complete_1 sk_toast_2) anteriority atom, although the passage supplies asserted events for the perfect to precede.

q2_gaps: day-of-year date numbering ("day 270 of Year 1") — the (Day <n>) term is specified as a calendar day paired with a month, so a day index with no month has no distinct encoding

transitive light verb over an event noun ("the village held the summer feast") — the light-verb rule names only intransitive occurred/happened/took place, leaving unsettled whether to reify a separate hold event or put the tense and Time terms on the feast witness

agent-nominalization taking an of-phrase ("the keepers of Aelmere") — it falls outside the nominalization-oblique rule's stated scope (act/result/quality nouns) yet passes that rule's verb-paraphrase test, while the Possession genitive is scoped to relational nouns with no underlying verb
review.notes: Compound decomposition (summer_feast), the Council-as-capitalized-common-noun default with no Name atom, the (Of sk_investiture_N …) nominalization oblique, and the group-only collective reading of "ate together" all follow the instruction set. (LocatedIn sk_square_1 sk_village_1) for "the village square" is licensed by the possessor/whole compound route plus the place-inside-a-place rule.

issues.reason: Real that the past perfect's anteriority goes unencoded, but overstated as a rule violation: the Time section's trigger reads "emit the ordering whenever the SENTENCE contains another asserted event for the perfect to precede ... a temporal clause, a causal one, or a relative clause", and this sentence holds only the completion event and is joined to the toasts by bare juxtaposition, so no stated rule names a pair to order and nothing emitted is false or over-asserted.

gaps_confirmed: day-of-year date numbering ("day 270 of Year 1") — the (Day <n>) term presupposes a day-of-month paired with a month, so a day index within a year has no distinct encoding

transitive light verb over an event noun ("the village held the summer feast") — the light-verb rule names only the intransitive occurred / happened / took place, leaving the reify-a-hold-event vs anchor-on-the-feast-witness choice unsettled

agent-nominalization taking an of-phrase ("the keepers of Aelmere") — the nominalization-oblique rule is scoped to act / result / quality nouns and the Possession genitive to relational nouns with no underlying verb, so neither branch cleanly covers an agent noun whose verb does exist
new_gaps: cross-sentence past-perfect anteriority in a passage — the ordering rule states its trigger over "the sentence" but its exclusion over "no other event in the text", and it supplies no way to choose WHICH prior event a discourse-level flashback joined only by juxtaposition should precede; a licensed form would need both a scope statement (sentence or passage) and an anchor-selection rule
adjudication.notes: The rest of the parse holds: the Council as a capitalized common noun with no Name atom, (LocatedIn sk_square_1 sk_village_1) for "the village square" under the place-inside-a-place rule, the collective reading of "ate together" with no per-member rule, summer_feast's genus with the noun modifier correctly unexposed, and the (Of sk_investiture_N ...) nominalization obliques. No atom is false, ill-typed, or over-asserted.
